messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Automated alert — repeated GPU driver resets (Xid 68) observed on node inference-prod-us-west-2-nn12. Severity: P1. Rolling error rate on serving runtime + spike in container OOMs. Alert details: <http://telemetry/internal/alerts/1719001234>

sre-maya: I'm taking this. pulling logs and checking node health now. anyone seeing similar across other nodes?

infra-ops: seeing correlated ECC/correctable counts across a small set of hosts in the same rack. quick paste from kernel + nvidia logs:```
Mar 15 02:14:22 nn12 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 68, PID 24321, GPU:0, Ch 00000010
Mar 15 02:14:22 nn12 containerd: oom-kill: container foo-service (pid 24321) total-vm: 1234567kB, anon-rss: 456789kB
Mar 15 02:14:22 nn12 nvidia-smi dmon -s u
#gpu pwr temp mem
0  85W  78C  98%
1  60W  70C  82%
```

eng-ryan: we also saw KV cache OOMs in the serving runtime right before the Xid flurry — that matches container restarts for the heavy-reuse shard. stack traces show `std::bad_alloc` from kvcache allocator in a few containers. not sure if it's driver-induced or actual host memory pressure.

sre-maya: good catch. running `free -m && slabtop` and checking host oom_kill logs. initial check: host memory looks fine but GPU memory shows sustained high usage on GPU0. preparing to cordon/evacuate node if resets continue.

support-julia: FYI two customers have opened tickets: `skywidgets` and `fasttext-ai`. Both report elevated latencies and intermittent 5xx errors starting ~02:10 UTC. Julia -> creating bridge with customers now.

cust-bridge: bridged with SkyWidgets support. They're seeing `502` and `context cancelled` from our API, roughly 30% of requests for embeddings for the past 20m. They've paused heavy batch jobs. Requested ETA on mitigation.

sre-maya: following runbook: `gpu-reset-xid` -> short checklist. 1) verify driver Xid pattern 2) attempt soft-evac 3) re-run diag. Link: <https://internal/runbooks/gpu-reset-xid> (reacted with :eyes:)

sre-maya: executing: `kubectl cordon inference-prod-us-west-2-nn12`
infra-ops: received cordon request, run `kubectl drain inference-prod-us-west-2-nn12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m` when ready.

sre-maya: drain started. evicting ~6 pods (mix of runtime and sidecars). command output:```
node/inference-prod-us-west-2-nn12 cordoned
pod/foo-service evicted
pod/bar-runtime evicted
...
```

eng-ryan: moving traffic: switching route for steady-state inferences to `inference-prod-us-west-2-fallback-1`. Will keep canary at 10% while we observe.

infra-ops: note: nv-host engine reports repeated `NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus` followed by `Xid 68`. Suspect transient PCI link or thermal excursion. Thermal graphs show GPU0 spiking to 85-88C during the flurry.

sre-mike: I'm joining for handoff. summary so far: node cordoned/draining, affected customers notified, traffic partially shifted. Next steps: run `nvidia-bug-report.sh` on node after it's drained and capture ECC counters, then attempt reboot-only, avoid driver reinstall mid-incident unless necessary. (reacted with :thumbsup:)

sre-maya: drain completed, migrated pods healthy on fallback. running `nvidia-bug-report.sh` now and collecting `/var/log/kern.log`. uploading bundle to ticket #INC-5871.

support-julia: relaying to SkyWidgets: we expect limited impact during migration; please resume validation and message if you still see >5% errors.

cust-bridge: SkyWidgets confirmed reduced errors to <3% after traffic shift, will keep tests running for 1 hour.

sre-mike: handoff notes for night SRE: node inference-prod-us-west-2-nn12 shows repeating Xid 68 tied to GPU0, high GPU temps, and container OOMs on heavy KV-cache workloads. Already cordoned and drained. Artifacts: bugreport + kernel logs uploaded to INC-5871. Recommended next steps for oncall: run vendor GPU diag (nvmsi health) tomorrow, consider hardware replacement if Xid recurs after reboot, and open vendor case if ECC counters keep rising. Escalation: hardware vendor + infra team. (reacted with :white_check_mark:)

sre-maya: leaving the channel. handing off to @sre-mike for overnight. Logging final note in incident tracker and will follow up in morning.

oncall-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged. Incident channel will remain open for updates.
